heard: In 1932, Australia went to war against birds, and lost. After World War I, the government gave veterans farmland in Western Australia. Then 20,000 emus showed up and started eating the wheat. So the farmers called the army. The army sent one major, two soldiers, two machine guns, and 10,000 bullets. The emus split into tiny groups and ran out of range, when a thousand of them finally walked into an ambush. The gun jammed, so they mounted a gun on a truck. The emus were faster than the truck. By December, nearly 10,000 bullets for 986 emus, 10 bullets per bird. The major's review of the enemy? They can face machine guns with the invulnerability of tanks. The army went home. The emus did not.
